newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings leads tight presidential race.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings leads tight presidential race.

text.p: Ghana's populist president Jerry Rawlings, who twice seized power before becoming an elected head of state in 1992, enjoyed a clear lead on Sunday in his bid for a final four-year term, partial results showed.
Provisional results from Saturday's national elections credited Rawlings with over 55 percent of the vote compared to less than 42 percent for his main rival, John Kufuor.
The results from the National Election Commission covered only 64 of Ghana's 200 constituencies but unofficial results from 126 constituencies confirmed the trend.
Supporters of Rawlings, who has been called everything from a dictator to a messiah, gathered outside the headquarters of his National Democratic Congress in festive mood.
"I am counting on at least 60 percent of the total votes to render a second round of no consequence," the 49-year-old Rawlings, who is half-Scottish, told Reuters earlier.

Kufuor, a politician and businessman who was celebrating his 58th birthday on Sunday, enjoyed landslides of his own in constituencies in and around his stronghold of Kumasi, Ghana's second town and capital of the pre-colonial Ashanti empire.
Political pundits said Rawlings appeared to be winning more of the rural vote, with Kufuor taking more of the urban vote.
The third contender, surgeon Edward Mahama of the People's National Convention, had just 2.58 percent of votes.

In the contest for parliament's 200 seats, which was being tallied separately, Rawlings's party had won 37 compared to 27 for Kufuor's New Patriotic Party and two for his People's Convention Party opposition allies, according to the commission.
Unofficial results credited Rawlings's party with 54 seats and the opposition alliance with 31.

Ghanaians voted peacefully and in large numbers. Election Commission chairman Kwadwo Afari-Gyan put the turnout at 70 percent. More than nine million of Ghana's 17.5 million people were eligible to vote.

The Commonwealth Observer Group, among around 100 foreign observers monitoring the poll, paid tribute to the organisation and conduct of the election. "We believe that the conditions existed for a free expression of will by the electors," the 23-member mission said in a statement on Sunday.
Rawlings seized power as an air force flight-lieutenant in 1979, executing three former heads of state. He restored civilian rule but seized power again in 1981.

A former socialist firebrand, he converted to Western-style free-market economics -- winning plaudits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. He made the transition to elected president in disputed 1992 elections.

The main opposition, campaigning under the banner of the Great Alliance, learned the lesson of going into the 1992 multi-party elections in disarray and, against the odds, formed a common front for this year's elections.
Kufuor, who trained as a lawyer, has been campaigning for Ghanaians to have a greater stake in Ghana's economy, in which cocoa-growing and gold-mining are prominent.
A key question was whether Rawlings's charisma would win him re-election in the face of widespread unemployment and high inflation which have fuelled popular discontent.
If neither candidate wins an overall majority, a run-off must be held within 21 days.
